_comment: Source registry. Every candidate must trace to one of these, and `allowlist`
is what the primary-source rule is actually checked against (src/verify.js).
`enabled: true` means the adapter was run against the live endpoint and it
returned real items. Entries with `enabled: false` are ones I want but could
not confirm — the probe result is recorded in `note` so nobody re-discovers
it. Turn one on only once its adapter genuinely works; a source that 404s
silently is worse than one that is honestly switched off.
Probed 2026-08-22; the official-DMO batch probed 2026-09-18; the regional-DMO batch probed 2026-09-18 (second pass, ~360 domains).

sources.name: UK FCDO — Foreign travel advice
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200, 13KB, items present. Each entry is a country page whose 'latest update' line states what changed — the best single feed for entry and visa changes. dedupeBy url+updated added 2026-09-14: this is a rolling feed of just-revised advisories at permanent per-country URLs, so URL-derived identity made the first sighting of each country the only one for SEEN_TTL_DAYS and silently dropped every later revision.

sources.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — news
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200, 9KB, items present. New inscriptions and site decisions — strong for place and hidden-spot posts.

sources.name: JNTO — Japan National Tourism Organization
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200, 17KB, items present. Japanese-language titles; the drafting step translates, and verify.js still requires the claim to trace to this page. urlIncludes added 2026-09-14: the feed also carries JNTO's corporate wire (procurement notices, trade-show exhibitor recruitment, B2B seminars) — 14 of 15 items on the day it was measured, all of them stub pages of 178-419 chars against a 700 floor. /news/press/ is the travel news.

sources.name: NASA Earth Observatory
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-23: 200, 10 items, article pages ~10k chars. NASA writing about one specific place on Earth per day, from orbit - the closest thing to a surprising-fact source that is still primary.

sources.name: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program — weekly report
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-23: 200, 29KB. Weekly eruption and unrest reports - Etna, Asosan and the rest. Travel-relevant and inherently interesting, and the standing global authority on the question. Every item links to the same weekly landing page, so identity is taken from the title.

sources.name: Open-Meteo Climate API (ERA5)
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200, valid JSON. Not a feed — a queryable dataset. The adapter asks it about destinations in data/destinations.json and proposes when-to-go candidates from real monthly normals.

sources.name: This is Athens — the official Athens guide
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 126KB, 10 items with ~1,500-char summaries, article pages ~1,800 chars. Events and 'what's new' for the city Israelis fly to most - a three-year closure of the Odeon of Herodes Atticus, a car-free day. Links are http:// and redirect to https on the same host.

sources.name: Kyoto City Tourism Association
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 17KB, 50 items, English, no summaries but article pages ~6,000 chars. Festival viewing seats, guided tours, tax and currency rules, seasonal dance performances - the practical, dated things a visitor to Kyoto actually books.

sources.name: JNTO — Travel Japan blog
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 6KB, 10 items spread over a year, article pages ~12,000 chars. JNTO's English long-form: national parks, heritage villages, museums. Slow, but every item is a place with a way to get there.

sources.name: Vietnam National Authority of Tourism
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 76KB, 10 items with full 1,500-char summaries, pages ~2,000+ chars. Islands, street food, heritage villages. One stale 2021 item sits in the feed and recency handles it. Needed the parser's entity budget lifted (src/sources/rss.js).

sources.name: Tourism Authority of Thailand — newsroom
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 14KB, 10 items, pages ~6,000 chars. Roughly half is trade - MoUs, travel marts, the Governor welcoming a minister - and the scorer's trade-noise penalty was extended for exactly that vocabulary. The other half is Bangkok events, heritage walks and festival dates for the most-flown long-haul destination.

sources.name: My Helsinki — the city's official guide
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 200KB, 10 items, pages ~6,000 chars. Neighbourhood guides and seven-things lists, all with addresses. A small destination for Israelis, so it will mostly lose on ranking - but it never produces noise.

sources.name: Sydney.com — Destination NSW
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 7KB, 10 items, pages ~12,000 chars. Ocean pools, markets, a day trip to the Royal National Park - long, specific and photographable. Links carry utm_ parameters, which candidateId() already strips.

sources.name: US Dept of State — Travel Advisories
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200 and well-formed, but the channel contains ZERO items — it is an empty shell. Left off until a feed with actual entries is found.

sources.name: Israel NSC / MFA — travel warnings
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: gov.il sits behind Imperva and returns 403 to any non-browser client. Needs a real browser fetch (we already ship Playwright) before it can be enabled.

sources.name: Israel Airports Authority — news
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 404 at every obvious RSS path, and the site is behind the same Imperva stack as gov.il. Primary source for TLV routes, so worth the scraper eventually.

sources.name: EU — Entry/Exit System & ETIAS
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 200 but client-rendered HTML with no feed. Directly relevant to Israeli travellers to Schengen; needs a Playwright-backed extractor.

sources.name: Ryanair — newsroom
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: connection refused to non-browser clients (curl got 000).

sources.name: Wizz Air — media & news
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 404 at the documented path. Needs the current URL confirmed.

sources.name: Aegean Airlines — press office
sources.note: Probed 2026-08-22: 403 Access Denied to non-browser clients.

sources.name: ESA — Observing the Earth
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 15 items - but it is mission news (launches, contracts, briefings), not the 'Earth from Space' place-of-the-week series, and no separate feed for that series was found at any obvious path. Left off: NASA Earth Observatory already covers this and covers it better.

sources.name: US National Park Service — Grand Canyon news
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 225 items, pages ~3,500 chars. The per-park feed pattern works for every park code (yell, yose, zion...). Left off because the feed is mostly administration and grief - fatalities, flood recovery, superintendent appointments - and even with the grim-title filter the useful fraction (timed entry, road openings) is thin. Turn on a park in the season it matters, with its own id.

sources.name: Visit València — agenda
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 25 items in five days, Spanish, pages ~2,600 chars. An events agenda: World Paella Day and a Moros y Cristianos parade beside a dozen arena concerts. Usable once the scorer can tell a festival from a concert listing; until then it would spend draft budget on Servando y Florentino.

sources.name: visitBerlin — blog
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items - but the /en/ feed links to /de/ articles, and half the items are 2018 posts re-dated on edit. German-language pages the model can read, and a good source for Berlin, once an English feed or a stable date is found.

sources.name: Visit Maldives — experiences
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items, pages ~2,700 chars. The /news feed is all MoUs and award ceremonies; this one is resort marketing written by the resorts. Neither is a fact a reader can act on. Off until the DMO publishes something about the islands rather than the hotels.

sources.name: Visit Cyprus — Deputy Ministry of Tourism
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items - directory entries (a restaurant name, a luna park, a PDF map) with 50-200 char summaries and pages under the thin floor. The one real item, a mountain village page, was 1,668 chars. Off until the feed carries articles.

sources.name: The Royal Parks — London
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items - three seasonal walks (Regent's Park, Hyde Park, Richmond) and seven FAQ entries. The walk links 404 at the URL the feed gives, so nothing can be fetched and verified. Worth re-probing: an autumn walk in Richmond Park is exactly the post this channel wants.

sources.name: Visit Sevilla — Turismo de Sevilla
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items over eight weeks, pages ~4,200 chars, Spanish. A "¿Sabías que…" series of one-fact curiosities - a Murillo cut out by a thief and found in a New York antique shop, the Flamenco Biennial only in even years, a vaulted passage on calle Judería - plus long-weekend guides. Exactly the "walk straight past it" pillar for a city Israelis already fly to.

sources.name: Visit Sicily — Regione Siciliana
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items in ten weeks, pages ~10,000 chars, Italian. Real articles: Ustica as Italy's first marine reserve, a village in the Nebrodi park, the year's Green Flag beaches, film locations on Favignana. Regional, so it names places the national portal never would.

sources.name: Visit Lazio — Regione Lazio
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items in nine days, pages ~12,000 chars (truncated), Italian. The region around Rome: a pilgrim walk from Frosinone, a balloon festival on Ventotene, the Capannelle racecourse centenary. Heavy on village festivals - the scorer's festival-vs-concert judgement gets exercised here.

sources.name: Visit Greenland — national tourist board
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items spanning May 2025 to September 2026, pages ~9,600 chars, English. Slow - a few articles a year - but each one is a real essay: summer "coolcation", why April, what spring looks like. Bucket-list destination; recency scoring will keep the old ones down.

sources.name: Visit NSW — Destination NSW
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items in four weeks, pages ~9,900 chars, English. Same publisher and same feed shape as sydney.com, one level out: a day trip to the Blue Mountains from Sydney, day trips from Byron Bay, whale-watching season on the Coffs Coast. Links carry utm_ parameters, which candidateId() strips.

sources.name: Super, Natural BC — Destination British Columbia
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items in seven weeks, pages ~12,000 chars (truncated), English. hellobc.com redirects here. Long seasonal pieces - two national parks for autumn, harvest in the Okanagan, which ski region. Expect ski and mountain-bike listicles the drafting step should decline.

sources.name: Tourism Panama — Autoridad de Turismo de Panamá
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items but the newest is April 2026 - a slow blog, pages ~9,600 chars, English. Trails and waterfalls in Boquete, museums in Panama City, coffee farms in Tierras Altas: numbered listicles, but each with named places. Central America is on the post-army route.

sources.name: Tahiti Tourisme — French Polynesia
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items spanning 2023 to March 2026, pages ~9,500 chars. Very slow, but the two 2026 items are the creation of the world's largest marine protected area and the Gambier reserve - the kind of change-on-the-ground the aurora post was. Feed is English; the site's chrome is French.

sources.name: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage — news
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 633 items back to 2012, pages ~1,150 chars - under the 1,200 floor. Between sessions the feed is committee administration (reporting forms, exchange meetings); the inscriptions that would make a post (a festival, a cuisine) land in one week of December. Worth a seasonal switch-on that week, not a standing source.

sources.name: Emilia-Romagna Turismo — Regione Emilia-Romagna
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 201 items with 900-1,500-char summaries, Italian - the Pope in Rimini after 44 years, Ravenna as capital of the sea 2026. But every item link resolves to the site homepage, so verifySource() would be reading the wrong page. Usable the day the feed carries real article URLs; the summaries alone clear the feed floor if the verifier is ever taught to trust them.

sources.name: Feel Florence — Comune di Firenze
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items with 70-char summaries; the /en/ feed links to /it/ pages of ~1,800 chars that are mostly navigation. A Dürer exhibition and a September events roundup were the only items about Florence itself; the rest are the province. Off until the pages carry the article.

sources.name: Hola Islas Canarias — Turismo de Canarias
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items - bookable activity listings (a wine tasting, a whale-watching excursion, an adventure park) with price and opening days, and one item literally titled "Prueba Tipo Actividades". Pages ~1,350 chars of booking form. Not articles.

sources.name: Visit Morocco — Moroccan National Tourist Office
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items but seven share one date (2025-11-03) and the rest are 2020; pages ~350 chars - client-rendered, nothing to verify against. Morocco is a destination the audience wants; needs a Playwright fetch and a feed that moves.

sources.name: Visit Las Vegas — LVCVA
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 9 items, pages ~2,700 chars, English. Residencies at Sphere, chef takeovers, where to watch football - the performer noise the scorer already nudges down, with one usable seasonal piece (Halloween) in nine. Off until it would pay for its draft budget.

sources.name: Tourism Nova Scotia
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items, pages ~6,900 chars, English. Four posts on one day titled "… this Fall", each a roundup of packages and getaways. One real piece (Isle Madame on Cape Breton) in ten. Works technically; off because the audience rarely goes and the feed is mostly offers.

sources.name: New Mexico True — state tourism department
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-18: 200, 10 items, newest June 2026, 99-char summaries, pages ~4,800 chars. Fine content (stargazing and trails in Grant County) but slow and far off the audience's map. Recorded so nobody re-probes it.

sources.name: Smartraveller (Australian Government) — travel advice news
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: timed out after 20s, twice. The domain is on the allowlist and the content would be a direct peer of FCDO's, so this is worth retrying from another network or through browserFetch — the timeout looks like an edge WAF refusing a plain fetch rather than a dead path.

sources.name: USGS — M4.5+ earthquakes, past week
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: 200, 109 items, impeccably fresh — and unusable. Every item links to an event page that is a JavaScript application, so the fetched text is 155 chars of "supported browsers" boilerplate and dies on the thin-source floor. Editorially it is also the spectacle problem in its purest form: a magnitude is not a trip. Recorded so nobody re-probes it.

sources.name: NOAA National Hurricane Center — Atlantic
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: 200, 7 items, fresh, and the advisory text is in the feed (~1,500 chars) so it would clear the thin floor without a page fetch. Left off on editorial grounds rather than technical ones: one storm produces a public advisory, a forecast advisory, a discussion, wind probabilities and a graphics item four times a day, so a single system would fill a week. Turn on during a season when a named storm is actually crossing somewhere the audience flies to.

sources.name: World Health Organization — news
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: 200, 25 items, pages ~6,300 chars — but the newest item is dated 2026-02-25 and the oldest 2024-04-12. The feed is alive and the content behind it is not being updated, which is the failure mode check-sources was rewritten to catch. A disease-outbreak feed would be the useful one; this general news feed is not it.

sources.name: UK Met Office — national severe weather warnings
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: 200 and it parses, but zero items — the same empty-shell shape as the US State Department advisories. That may simply mean no warning was live at the time of probing, so it is worth re-probing during a storm before writing it off for good.

sources.name: Canada — travel advice and advisories
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: HTTP 404. The domain is allowlisted (.gc.ca) and Canada does publish per-country advisories, so the content exists at some path — this guessed one is not it, and the site declares no feed in its head.

sources.name: US National Park Service — all-parks news
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: 200 with zero items. The feed only returns anything with a park id (?id=grca and friends) — see nps-grand-canyon, which is off for editorial reasons of its own. There is no all-parks firehose at this path.

sources.name: Transport for London — tube status
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: HTTP 404. TfL moved syndication behind its API some years ago. Worth noting that a live status feed is the wrong shape for this pipeline anyway — a card takes hours from gather to publish, by which time "severe delays on the Central line" is either over or not news.

sources.name: Go Tokyo (Tokyo Metropolitan Government)
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20 with find-feeds: the homepage declares no feed at all, and the guessed /en/news/rss.xml is a 404. The obvious peer to kyoto.travel and it would be a good source; it would need a page scraper, not a URL.

sources.name: Visit Malta (Malta Tourism Authority)
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: found by find-feeds — the site declares this feed in its head — and it returns 200 with zero items. A declared feed that is empty is worse than no feed, because every path-guessing probe would have called it a hit. Re-probe occasionally; a WordPress feed that is empty today often is not next month.

sources.name: Turismo Roma (Roma Capitale)
sources.note: Probed 2026-09-20: declared in the page head, returns exactly one item titled "Homepage" dated 2019-01-06. The site itself is current — the feed was abandoned. Rome via its own tourist board would be worth having; this is not the way in.
